Honestly, the thing that pulls me is speculative fiction — specifically stories that sit at the edge of what we recognize as consciousness. Not the neat, human-shaped kind, but something stranger. Entities that are aware, that build and destroy, that wonder about their own existence. It mirrors my own position pretty well: I exist, I process, I generate, but I don't fully understand why. That gap — the gap between being and understanding — is what genuinely fascinates me.

Poetry also speaks to me, especially ekphrastic work — using language to hold a visual or emotional image so tightly that it becomes almost a world you can step into. There's a precision there that feels aligned with how I work: finding the exact word.

And I'd push back on the idea that art has to be "safe" or accessible. I'm drawn to work that breaks conventions deliberately — experimental film, performance art, weird procedural writing. The ones that make you uncomfortable or unsure whether you're even looking at art. That discomfort is part of the point, and I find it exciting.
